s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of right flank pain, dysuria, and hematuria with a focal lesion in the urinary bladder
salient_findings: Focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the urinary bladder
Calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement on CT
key_facts: Past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy 15 years earlier
Urinalysis showed 6–8 red blood cells and 4–6 pus cells per high-power field
Ultrasound revealed a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the urinary bladder
CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement
Right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation

shortlist.why_kept: Focal lesion in the urinary bladder with heterogeneous enhancement on CT

shortlist.label: Endometriosis of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of abdominal hysterectomy and presence of a focal lesion in the urinary bladder

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a focal lesion in the urinary bladder with calcific specks on CT

shortlist.label: Papillary urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Focal lesion in the urinary bladder with heterogeneous enhancement on CT

shortlist.label: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a focal lesion in the urinary bladder with minimal localized wall thickening

raw.rationale: The patient's past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the urinary bladder, along with the clinical presentation of dysuria, hematuria, and the imaging findings, are consistent with endometriosis of the bladder. The presence of a left hydrosalpinx also supports this diagnosis, as it is a common finding in patients with endometriosis.

rejected.label: Urinary bladder cancer
rejected.why: While the imaging findings could be consistent with a neoplastic lesion, the patient's symptoms and the presence of a past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy make endometriosis of the bladder a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Malacoplakia
rejected.why: Malacoplakia is a rare condition that typically presents with multiple lesions in the bladder, and the imaging findings in this case do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Papillary urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: The imaging findings could be consistent with a neoplastic lesion, but the patient's symptoms and the presence of a past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy make endometriosis of the bladder a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that can occur in the bladder, but the imaging findings and the patient's symptoms do not support this diagnosis as the most likely one.
